newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana parishes to vote Saturday on bonds, tax.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana parishes to vote Saturday on bonds, tax.

text.p: Voters in several Louisiana parishes will vote Saturday on local bond and tax issues, The Advocate newspaper reported.
In Iberville Parish, voters will decide whether to retain their police jury or replace it with a parish council form of government established through a home rule charter.

In the past few years, voters in Livingston, West Baton Rouge and Ascension parishes have adopted the latter. Under the parish council government, the council president acts as chief executive and administers parish government while the council has legislative authority, adopting budgets and ordinances.

If voters approve, the parish will hold a special election to choose a council president in the spring, while incumbent police jurors would serve the remainder of their terms as parish counsil members.
Lafourche Parish voters will decide wheter to issue $44.4 million of 20-year bonds for schools. The debt would be repaid with current property taxes.
Lafourche Parish is also asking rural voters to approve a half-cent sales tax hike for the sheriff's department. Voters rejected similar proposals six months ago and in 1988 and 1983.
Sheriff Craig Webre said if the proposal fails, the 194-member department would be forced to cut 20 percent of its employees. The tax would raise $2.4 million a year.
In Livingston Parish, City of Watson residents will vote on a proposed half-cent sales tax increase that would generate $130,000 a year for drainage.

St. James Parish will vote on a proposal to extend its law enforcment property tax to raise sheriff's deputies' pay. The 10-year, 12.5 mill tax would replace an existing 6-mill taz that expires next year. The increase would generate an additional $1.3 million annually.

In St. Tammany Parish, voters in the Mandeville area will vote on two proposals for Gravity Drainage District 4. One would authorize a $5 million issue of 20-year bonds and the other would implement a 10-year, 4-mill property tax to build and operate drainage works.
In West Feliciana Parish, St. Francisville precints will consider four tax restructuring proposals and voters in unincorproated areas will decide five. They are:
--an 8.89 mill tax increase for five years requested by the police jury for roads, public buildings and recreation programs.
--a 0.25-mill, five-year tax for the parish health unit.
--a 0.1-mill tax for five years to fund socal services agencies and programs.
--a $10 million, 15-year bond issue for the West Feliciana Parish School Board to build a middle school and removate two elemenatry schools.
--in unincorporated areas, Fire Protection Distric 1 would cut its 6.77-mill property tax to 2.4 mills for five years.
